aweme_info.content_desc: ["here’s the guide \ud83d\udcaa it's called body recomposition (losing fat while building muscle at the same time). for everyone asking how, here's what helped me!! 1. diet: prioritize protein in every meal and eat good quality carbs like sweet potatoes, rice, and oats. if fat loss is your goal, a small calorie deficit will help. 2. workouts: lift weights 3-5 times a week. don't just copy random influencer workouts or train without a plan. follow a structured routine and focus on progressive overload. 3. coaching or apps: SO helpful!! i followed the weight loss program in Vanholt Fitness app. it builds a personalized workout plan based on your starting physique, goals and equipment. it also has exercise tutorials, progressive overload tracking and calorie \u0026 macro tracking! 4. patience: you can't choose where you lose fat (arms, legs, stomach, etc.), but you CAN build specific muscles through targeted exercises. that's why having a structured plan matters!! 5. sleep: aim for 8+ hours a night. recovery is just as important as training!!","save this for later and remember, consistency is everything \ud83e\udef6\ud83d\udc97"]
aweme_info.desc: here’s the guide 💪 it's called body recomposition (losing fat while building muscle at the same time). for everyone asking how, here's what helped me!! 1. diet: prioritize protein in every meal and eat good quality carbs like sweet potatoes, rice, and oats. if fat loss is your goal, a small calorie deficit will help. 2. workouts: lift weights 3-5 times a week. don't just copy random influencer workouts or train without a plan. follow a structured routine and focus on progressive overload. 3. coaching or apps: SO helpful!! i followed the weight loss program in Vanholt Fitness app. it builds a personalized workout plan based on your starting physique, goals and equipment. it also has exercise tutorials, progressive overload tracking and calorie & macro tracking! 4. patience: you can't choose where you lose fat (arms, legs, stomach, etc.), but you CAN build specific muscles through targeted exercises. that's why having a structured plan matters!! 5. sleep: aim for 8+ hours a night. recovery is just as important as training!! save this for later and remember, consistency is everything 🫶💗

here’s the guide 💪 it's called body recomposition (losing fat while building muscle at the same time). for everyone asking how, here's what helped me!! 1. diet: prioritize protein in every meal and eat good quality carbs like sweet potatoes, rice, and oats. if fat loss is your goal, a small calorie deficit will help. 2. workouts: lift weights 3-5 times a week. don't just copy random influencer workouts or train without a plan. follow a structured routine and focus on progressive overload. 3. coaching or apps: SO helpful!! i followed the weight loss program in Vanholt Fitness app. it builds a personalized workout plan based on your starting physique, goals and equipment. it also has exercise tutorials, progressive overload tracking and calorie & macro tracking! 4. patience: you can't choose where you lose fat (arms, legs, stomach, etc.), but you CAN build specific muscles through targeted exercises. that's why having a structured plan matters!! 5. sleep: aim for 8+ hours a night. recovery is just as important as training!!
save this for later and remember, consistency is everything 🫶💗

Some hunger during weight loss is normal, but we shouldn’t act like it’s a necessary pre-requisite (or even a badge of honour).

Weight loss shouldn’t be able ravenous hunger 24/7. The focus should be on building Hunger Crushing Combos that help you maintain a calorie deficit while staying full. I have a full chapter on this in my book if you want more guidance.

What are your thoughts on hunger and weight loss? #weightloss #dietitian #nutrition

aweme_info.desc: DM me the word 'PLATES’ on my IG and I’ll send you my training on how to eat more to lose fat after 35. If you’re a high-performing woman who’s doing everything right and your body still isn’t reacting like it used to, the plate is the first place to look. Why each pick lands where it does: Carbs: Rice on its own digests fast and leaves you hungry again. Oats and potatoes keep your blood sugar steady, so you’re not digging through the pantry at 3pm. Fats: Trail mix is mostly candy and dried fruit, and it disappears fast while you answer emails. Almonds come with fiber and protein. Salmon adds protein and omega-3 fats that keep you full for hours. Drinks: A restaurant margarita can run 300 to 500 calories with a sugar crash on top. Dry white wine and a vodka soda with lime sit around 100 to 120 with no sugar. Alcohol still pauses fat burning, so pick your drink on purpose. Olive oil: A shot on an empty stomach is 120 calories of fat with nothing to keep you full. A tablespoon on your veggies, or a few sprays from a mister, gets you the benefit without the guessing. Lunch: The plain desk salad is usually behind the 9pm pantry raid. Add protein and a real carb and the afternoon changes. Nothing here asks you to eat less. The effortless foods fill you up and steady your blood sugar, which lets you eat more while your metabolism rebuilds. DM me the word "PLATES” on my IG and I’ll send it over. original_client_text.markup_text:
DM me the word 'PLATES’ on my IG and I’ll send you my training on how to eat more to lose fat after 35.

If you’re a high-performing woman who’s doing everything right and your body still isn’t reacting like it used to, the plate is the first place to look.

Why each pick lands where it does:

Carbs: Rice on its own digests fast and leaves you hungry again.
Oats and potatoes keep your blood sugar steady, so you’re not digging through the pantry at 3pm.

Fats: Trail mix is mostly candy and dried fruit, and it disappears fast while you answer emails. Almonds come with fiber and protein. Salmon adds protein and omega-3 fats that keep you full for hours.

Drinks: A restaurant margarita can run 300 to 500 calories with a sugar crash on top. Dry white wine and a vodka soda with lime sit around 100 to 120 with no sugar.

Alcohol still pauses fat burning, so pick your drink on purpose.

Olive oil: A shot on an empty stomach is 120 calories of fat with nothing to keep you full. A tablespoon on your veggies, or a few sprays from a mister, gets you the benefit without the guessing.

Lunch: The plain desk salad is usually behind the 9pm pantry raid. Add protein and a real carb and the afternoon changes.

Nothing here asks you to eat less. The effortless foods fill you up and steady your blood sugar, which lets you eat more while your metabolism rebuilds.

DM me the word "PLATES” on my IG and I’ll send it over.

Save this workout and do it 4× a week using light weights.

aweme_info.desc: Eating less isn't always the answer. For years, we've been told that if we want to lose weight, we need to eat less. So we skip meals, cut portions, avoid carbs and try to get by on as little food as possible. But here's where that approach can backfire, especially in midlife. When you're constantly trying to eat less, you're often missing out on the very things that make fat loss easier to manage. Protein to help keep you full and maintain muscle. Fibre to support digestion, gut health and keep hunger in check. Food volume, so you can eat satisfying meals without consuming excessive calories. And when you're hungry all the time, it's much harder to stick to your calorie goals. You end up snacking, picking at food or overeating later in the day. The answer isn't to keep cutting calories. It's to make the calories you're eating work harder for you. Build your meals around protein, add plenty of fibre-rich foods and fill your plate with foods that give you more volume for fewer calories. You still need a calorie deficit to lose fat, but you don't need to spend your days feeling hungry and deprived. Eating smarter, not just eating less, can make all the difference. Follow me for practical nutrition and fat loss advice for women in midlife. #MenopauseWeightLoss #FatLossOver50 #MidlifeNutrition #MacroNutrition #WomenOver50

original_client_text.markup_text:
Eating less isn't always the answer.
For years, we've been told that if we want to lose weight, we need to eat less.
So we skip meals, cut portions, avoid carbs and try to get by on as little food as possible.
But here's where that approach can backfire, especially in midlife.
When you're constantly trying to eat less, you're often missing out on the very things that make fat loss easier to manage.
Protein to help keep you full and maintain muscle.
Fibre to support digestion, gut health and keep hunger in check.
Food volume, so you can eat satisfying meals without consuming excessive calories.
And when you're hungry all the time, it's much harder to stick to your calorie goals. You end up snacking, picking at food or overeating later in the day.
The answer isn't to keep cutting calories.
It's to make the calories you're eating work harder for you.
Build your meals around protein, add plenty of fibre-rich foods and fill your plate with foods that give you more volume for fewer calories.
You still need a calorie deficit to lose fat, but you don't need to spend your days feeling hungry and deprived.
Eating smarter, not just eating less, can make all the difference.
Follow me for practical nutrition and fat loss advice for women in midlife.
#MenopauseWeightLoss #FatLossOver50 #MidlifeNutrition #MacroNutrition #WomenOver50
